Mutations in PIGA disrupt the initial step of GPI biosynthesis. This leads to a failure in producing functional GPI anchors, which are essential for cell surface expression of numerous proteins. In multiple congenital anomalies-hypotonia-seizures syndrome 2, this broad disruption of GPI-anchored proteins likely affects multiple developmental processes. In paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria 1, the lack of GPI anchors specifically impairs the surface expression of complement regulatory proteins like CD55 and CD59 on red blood cells, leading to their increased susceptibility to complement-mediated lysis and subsequent hemolysis.
